title: Spring Spin
subtitle: a discount game to win new clients

steps.title: You work with AI. It reports progress as it goes.
steps.note: The agent builds Spring Spin and records each step in Techlog, instead of waiting for a review to explain it.

lines.x: Sent by the agent over MCP, one call per step.

steps.title: The old way: the change waits for a review.
steps.note: Reviewers get a diff but not the reasons, so they ask, wait for answers, and ask again.

lines.x: The answers already exist as linked events:
Approved with finance: 20% cap, two-week window

steps.title: Techlog finds the connections.
steps.note: Each event is checked against the schema, then linked to what it implements, decides, and verifies. Nobody types the links by hand.

lines.x: The diff shows which lines changed.
It does not show the problem, the decision, or the test evidence.

steps.title: The discussion is gone.
steps.note: The reviewer opens one card with the why, the approval, and the evidence, and approves.

lines.x: Why: sign-ups flat for three weeks (evt_01J9K2A0P002)
Risk: stacking with other promotions, blocked

steps.title: Progress keeps flowing, even when it goes wrong.
steps.note: The canary release raises errors. Techlog links the incident to the release and the change, then the rollback to both.

lines.x: In a PR thread this is a new conversation, far from the code.
caused by the change (hypothesis, confirmed later by evt_01J9K2A0P015)

steps.title: One record for the whole team.
steps.note: Make your work with AI, and bring the progress to Techlog. Everyone reads the same linked story.

lines.x: The history is a comment thread.
Engineering: the change and its tests
Production: the release and the rollback
Support: the mitigation and its follow-ups (evt_01J9K2A0P024)
